summary: A brick light at the Potomac's mouth, built 1830 and darkened in 1966; a state park now opens its restored lighthouse for tours.

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel placed 1857 (LighthouseFriends); the USLHS record lists the current optic as removed.

structures.note: Brick dwelling with a lantern, built into the house; expanded to two full stories in 1883 (state). The state calls it the oldest integral lighthouse standing in the country.
Built in late 1965 off the point; worked with the lighthouse until January 1966 (state).

access.note: Point Lookout State Park; the lighthouse is open for tours on a seasonal schedule (state, 2025).

events.note: Built by John Donahoo for $3,350; original story and a half (Maryland DNR).
First lit by James Davis on 20 September 1830 (state); LighthouseFriends gives 30 September 1830.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens placed in the lantern.
House expanded to two full stories; light raised to 41 feet above sea level (state). The USLHS record gives 37 feet above water.
Station made a buoy depot with coal and buoy sheds and a wharf.
Funds for rebuilding the depot wharf provided.
Ice chafed the depot wharf piles in the severe winter of 1892-93; 38 piles covered with yellow metal (April 1893).
Iron oil house of about 1,000 gallons purchased for the station.
Red sector in the light discontinued 30 November 1895.
Keeper Thomas Jacobson towed a disabled U.S. Navy hydroplane (C-1) to shore on 25 July.
Keeper Thomas Jacobson transferred and promoted to mate of Cape Lookout Shoals Light Vessel No. 80, N.C.
Keeper G. M. Willis Sr. helped the captain of a beached schooner on 29 January (stored property, lodged crew).
Keeper Willis assisted occupants of a house destroyed by fire near the station (15 March).
Keeper Willis assisted an airplane and its occupants (index; LighthouseFriends dates it to 1925).
Centennial improvements: dwelling remodelled; wind-electric generating plant installed.
Oil-engine generators and new electrical equipment superseded the wind-electric plant.
Station transferred to the Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends).
Skeletal structure built off the point in late 1965; worked with the lighthouse until January 1966 (state). The USLHS record lists 1965 as the year it was discontinued.
Lighthouse darkened for the final time on 11 January 1966 by Raymond Hartzel.
State acquired the lighthouse from the U.S. Navy in a land swap.
Renovation began (state estimate of about $5 million total).
Reopened to visitors on Thursday, 15 May 2025, tours Thursday through Monday, hours seasonal.

corrections.why: The state's history says the lighthouse was darkened for the final time on 11 January 1966. The 1965 date in the record matches the offshore skeletal structure built that year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1965 entries mark the offshore skeletal structure built in late 1965. The lighthouse itself was darkened on 11 January 1966 (state history), which is the date the story uses.
The Archive gives 1831 for the light station's establishment and 1830 for the tower; the state and LighthouseFriends give 1830 for the building. The story gives both.
The state gives 41 feet (12 m) above sea level after the 1883 raising; the Archive gives 37 feet (11 m) above water. The story states both and does not choose.

The state dates the expansion into a duplex to 1927 (and its news release gives kitchen and dining rooms in 1927); the 1930 Bulletin article and LighthouseFriends date the centennial remodel to 1930. The story states both.
The Archive gives 1965 as the year discontinued; the state gives 11 January 1966 as the final darkening, after a skeletal structure worked with the lighthouse in late 1965. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: First lighting: the state gives 20 September 1830 and LighthouseFriends 30 September 1830; both are in the story. Height: the state says the light was raised to 41 feet above sea level in 1883; the USLHS record gives 37 feet above water; the station record gives a focal height of 6.1 m (about 20 ft) from the Light List. These are not reconciled. Remodel: the state says the dwelling was expanded in 1927 into a duplex; the Bulletin's 1930 'centennial improvements' article and LighthouseFriends describe the remodel as 1930. Not reconciled. Roster versus the state: Metivier keeper 1942 (roster) or 1943 (state); Gatton 1956 (roster) or 1957 (state). The roster lines are used as printed; both versions are in the story. Tower 2: Rowlett's 1965 'Tower 2' and the state's late-1965 skeletal structure are assumed to be the same thing, but the sources do not say so. The Bulletin's 1913 entry (Jacobson and the C-1 hydroplane) gives '25 July' with the year taken from the Bulletin volume. The 1919 schooner's name is garbled in the OCR and is left out. The 1891 wharf funds line carries an OCR-damaged date and is quoted without the date. Keepers under USCG (1949 to 1964) are in the roster as 'other' with the USLHS role note. Wikipedia was not used. No NRHP number is recorded in the station file, and none was checked. The newspaper search was not run for this station. Accessed dates use the system date, 2026-10-28. Checker notes (2026-10-27): (1) The 1894 oil-house entry (Board report for fiscal 1894, entry 464) reads 'was purchased and will be erected at the station'; the story says the Board bought it in the year ended 30 June 1894, not in 1894 by calendar year. LighthouseFriends dates the erection to 1895; the 1896 report says it was erected in June 1895. (2) The 1891 wharf-funds sentence was read in full: the funds 'having been provided on September 25, 1890'. (3) The Bulletin 1913 C-1 entry was read on its PDF page (page 35): 'On July 25, Thomas Jacobson, keeper of Point Lookout Light Station, Md., went to the assistance...'. (4) The Bulletin 1917 promotion (PDF page 31) reads 'transferred and promoted from keeper of Point Lookout Light Station, Md., to mate of Cape Lookout Shoals Light Vessel No. 80'. (5) The 1919 schooner entry (PDF page 12) was read in full; the schooner name is OCR-garbled and omitted. (6) The index entry for Willis and airplane 96 is on PDF page 36 of the 1924-1929 index. (7) The 1896 report carries the red-sector change in its changes list on scan page 26 as well as its entry on scan page 102; both are cited. (8) Disagreements now stated in the story: year established 1831 (Archive) against 1830 (state); height 41 ft (state) against 37 ft (Archive); the 1927 duplex versus the 1930 remodel; and the 1965 discontinuance (Archive) against 11 January 1966 (state).
